extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants and patent attorneys seeking French national patent or utility certificate protection
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to obtain and prosecute French national patents and certificates of utility, covering filing, priority, formal and substantive examination, searches, conversion, publication, opposition, limitation, invalidation, and related procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing language and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application can be filed in any language but a French translation is required within two months following receipt of a Communication issued by the French Patent Office (INPI) shortly after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be filed in docx format via the INPI e-procedure. It is possible to obtain a filing date even if no claims are filed (applicant invited to file claims within 2 months from receipt of a communication). No power of attorney is needed to authorize the attorney filing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining a filing date by reference to an earlier application
rubrics_metrics.description: A filing date can be obtained by mere reference to an earlier-filed application in a Paris Convention country, provided that the country, number and filing date of the earlier application are provided to the French Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within four months the applicant must submit a certified copy of the earlier patent application and its translation into French.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor designation deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventors must be designated no later than 16 months after the application date or the (earliest) priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inventor designation is filed within 16 months to meet formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim timing and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If priority is claimed under the Paris Convention, the FR application should be filed within 12 months of the earliest priority date and the date and country of the priority application(s) should be submitted at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certified copy of the priority application must be filed within 16 months of the earliest priority date, together with an English (or French) translation of the front page. INPI participates in DAS (since Dec 1, 2020) allowing automatic retrieval from participating offices. Restoration of priority may be possible up to 14 months in some error cases; adding a missing priority claim may be possible within 16 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination (what is checked)
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal examination is carried out by INPI before a prior art search to check compliance with formal requirements (e.g. adequate support for the claims in the specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal examination also determines whether claims are clear, cover only one invention, and whether the claimed invention is patentable subject matter. French patentable subject matter follows the EPC: programs for computers as such and business methods are not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention requires all claims to be linked by a common inventive concept; provisions same as in the EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent claims of the same category are prohibited except in specific situations (interrelated products; different solutions to the same particular problem; different uses). It's possible to include product, process and use claims linked by the product's original features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The search fee must be paid upon filing or within a time limit of 1 month from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late payment with surcharge is possible within two months following receipt of an official communication on late payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search procedure and preliminary search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results are issued as a 'preliminary search report' with written opinion, having the same structure as a European or PCT search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For first filings (no priority), the EPO often conducts the search as subcontractor and the extended preliminary search report is usually sent within ~9 months. When priority is claimed, INPI uses a two-step procedure (information on prior art then preliminary search report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step search procedure when priority is claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: I) About two years after the priority date INPI invites the applicant to provide information on documents cited in relation to applications sharing the same priority; II) Taking that information into account INPI carries out the search and issues the preliminary search report with written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response to the stage I invitation must be filed within 2 months (extendable once by 2 months). Replying is mandatory but there are no sanctions for failure; it serves to guide INPI's search. Amended claims can be filed together with the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between patent and certificate of utility
rubrics_metrics.description: A French Patent application may be converted into a Utility Certificate application at any time within 18 months from its filing date or, if a priority is claimed, from the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For conversion into a Patent from a Utility Certificate, the search fee must be paid within one month from the conversion request. Provisional applications have separate conversion rules (within one year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All French national patent applications are published 18 months after the filing date or the (earlier) priority date. Early publication can be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the preliminary search report is issued after publication of the application, the search report is published separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party observations (timing and anonymity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may file observations within 3 months from publication of the preliminary search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous observations are not accepted; third-party observations may affect substantive examination and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to the Preliminary Search Report (compulsory when relevant documents cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is compulsory to file a response to the preliminary search report within a (renewable) time limit of 3 months when documents are cited in a relevant category (mainly: noted “X” or “Y”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits vary by filing-date rules (see inventive-step changes); Examiner may issue Communication of non-compliance if grounds to reject. Typical reply time set by Office is normally two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection (pre- and post- May 22, 2020)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before May 22, 2020 INPI's grounds for rejection did not include lack of inventive step; for applications filed on May 22, 2020 and later lack of inventive step is a ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are invited to use the 'problem-solution' approach for assessing inventive step (similar to EPO). In both situations INPI may reject for new matter, lack of enablement or lack of unity. Divisional application filing date rules affect applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of new matter and claim amendment flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter can be introduced in any claim amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is slightly more flexibility for amendments than at the EPO, but introduced subject-matter is prohibited. When Examiner issues Communication of non-compliance, the usual time limit to reply is two months (renewable by Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination and final search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination is carried out based on the prior art cited in the preliminary search report, possible third party observations and responses by the Applicant; a final search report is then drawn up by the Examiner and appended to the granted patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final report reveals which documents the Examiner believes might affect validity of claims; this is published with the granted patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of examination (fast-track) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceleration requests are possible (since December 2015) and shall be made within 10 months from filing and include a request for early publication (if not already published). No official fee is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be accepted the application must be in condition for rapid examination: claims must be clear enough for a complete preliminary search report. Requesting an extension of a time limit for responding to an office action risks cancellation of accelerated proceedings. INPI endeavours to complete examination within 20 months but exceptions apply (objections, third-party observations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) availability and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH is available under a pilot program with the JPO (Japanese priority or PCT to Japanese national phase); PPH request is available as long as substantial examination of the French application has not started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No official fee; INPI recommends filing the PPH request within 12 months from filing. Required elements include: (1) claim correspondence table or statement claims are identical; (2) copies of relevant JPO office actions; (3) translations of such office actions; (4) copies of claims determined patentable by JPO; (5) translations of those claims; (6) copies of references cited by JPO if non-patent literature. If admissible, examination is expedited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection appeal route
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent application is rejected, the Applicant may initiate an Appeal against the decision before the Paris Court of Appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely lodging of appeals and compliance with appeal procedures governed by French courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant formalities and publication with final search report
rubrics_metrics.description: When the final search report is drawn up, the Applicant is invited to pay the grant and printing fees; the granted patent is published with the final search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication with the final search report informs the public about documents considered relevant by the Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant opposition (availability, timing, grounds and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition procedure implemented in 2020 and available for any French Patent granted on April 1, 2020 or later. Within 9 months from publication of the grant any third party can file an opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include lack of patentability, lack of enablement (insufficient disclosure) and extension of the scope of the granted patent. Procedure comprises a written phase and oral proceedings; patentee can respond and INPI issues a Preliminary Opinion; decision expected within ~4 months from oral proceedings and total duration ~16 months. Parties may appeal to the Paris Court of Appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant limitation procedure and acceptance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a French national patent (or the French part of a European patent) can request limitation at INPI; in Court-challenged validity cases, limitation may be requested and Court proceedings will be stayed until INPI decides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitation must amend at least one claim to limit its scope; amendment may find basis in the claims or description. INPI criteria: whether the claims are indeed limited and whether the amendments find clear basis in the patent. Patentee need not provide reasons for limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation (how and when to seek)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidation of a patent is generally requested as a counter-claim in infringement suits or may be initiated as a main claim before the Court; the filer must show an interest to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation actions are handled by French courts; enforcement and nullity issues are typically litigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territory covered by a French patent or certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: A French patent provides effect in France, as well as in the French overseas departments and territories, except for French Polynesia unless an extension fee is paid at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same territorial coverage applies to Certificates of Utility. Be aware to pay extension fee at filing to cover French Polynesia (since Feb 2014).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional patent application concept and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A French Provisional patent application may be filed without claims and without paying any fees except the filing fee; it is not published and is automatically deemed withdrawn after one year unless converted into a regular French Patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications may serve as the priority application for a subsequent patent application. If the Provisional claims the priority of a previous filing it cannot be handled as provisional and is automatically converted into a regular Patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional filing formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Provisional patent application may be filed without claims or abstract. There is no requirement to designate inventors. Only the filing fee is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File via INPI e-procedure. No examination is carried out on provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion rules for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year from filing the Provisional patent application, the Applicant may request its conversion into either a regular Patent application or into a Certificate of Utility application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provisional is automatically converted due to claiming priority of a previous filing, applicant is invited to pay the search fee or request conversion into a Certificate of Utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Utility filing and search fee rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for filing a Certificate of Utility are the same as for a patent application, except that no search fee is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal examination is the same as for a patent application; conversion between utility certificate and patent possible within 18 months (search fee due upon conversion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Utility duration and subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of utility have a maximum duration of 10 years and can cover a product, a method, or a device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subject matter fits statutory scope for utility certificates; renewals/term limited to 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, third-party observations and acceleration for utility certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: All French certificates of utility are published 18 months after filing or priority; third parties may file observations within 3 months from publication; acceleration of examination is available under the same conditions as for patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous observations not accepted. Applicant is invited to pay grant and printing fees after checking for observations. There is no post-grant opposition for utility certificates, but post-grant limitation is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation and enforceability of utility certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: To enforce a certificate of utility, the owner must request a prior art search at INPI. Invalidation can be requested as a counter-claim in infringement suits or as a main claim in an invalidation suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings for enforceability require an INPI prior-art search; invalidation handled by courts similar to patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coexistence of Certificate of Utility and Patent (double patenting risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: No clear legal basis excludes coexistence of a French Certificate of Utility and a French patent covering the same invention, but INPI may consider that an invention can be protected by one title only and is likely to issue a 'double patenting objection' asking the Applicant to abandon one of such titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two titles do not have the same effective date, the earlier effective date may anticipate the later. When filing both, prepare to address double patenting objections or choose the appropriate title.
